subject: Oceanography
title: Kelvin and Rossby Waves
description: A quick, practical guide to Kelvin and Rossby Waves.

hook.text: Some ocean waves take months to cross the Pacific—they are so long and slow you'd never notice them.

buildup.text: Kelvin waves travel along coastlines or the equator, guided by Earth's rotation.

discovery.text: Rossby waves move westward across entire ocean basins, driven by the Coriolis effect changing with latitude.

twist.text: Rossby waves take years to cross the Pacific—they carry climate signals across oceans.

climax.text: El Niño events involve equatorial Kelvin waves bouncing across the Pacific—connecting weather worldwide.

punchline.text: The slowest ocean waves carry the biggest climate messages.

quiz.question: What guides Kelvin waves along their path?
options: Earth's rotation and coastlines or the equator
